rationale: This engineering thesis compares two technical risk-analysis methods (consequence frequency assessment and computer modelling with probabilistic risk analysis) to estimate turbidity exceedance probabilities in a dual media rapid gravity filtration unit. Although the title mentions "non-compliant drinking water," compliance serves solely as a technical turbidity threshold for unit-process filtration modelling rather than a legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism governing household or community water service access (E06).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both the narrow and plain readings of Criterion 2 because the thesis is purely a water-treatment unit-process engineering and computer-modelling study of rapid gravity filtration turbidity risk, with no legal, administrative, institutional, or governance mechanism and no household/community service access dimension.

evidence_quotes.quote: Focusing on dual media rapid gravity filtration
evaluate the probability of producing non-compliant drinking water from a rapid gravity filtration unit with respect to turbidity.
The risk analysis methodologies that were used in this research were the consequence frequency assessment and computer modelling combined with probabilistic risk analysis.
